shots.action: Night, a hard wind. The hut heaves on its raft under three swinging lamps, the mooring rope bar-tight off the corner; the young man braces at the post, staring at it. The rope parts and whips; the hut lurches away and he throws his arms out, mouth open
shots.camera: Low and wide from the sea, pushing in

shots.action: Close on the mooring post: the frayed end thrashes on it while the rest of the rope slides off into black water with a splash. He lunges, one arm out, eyes wide, too late
shots.camera: Close and low at the corner of the raft

shots.action: Close on his face at the rail, eyes wide, mouth working, lamp light swinging across it. Behind him a crow in a long coat flaps down onto the roof ridge and folds his arms
From high up: the hut slides away into the dark, lamps burning; the lights of the other huts shrink behind it. He is at the back rail with both arms up, shouting after them
shots.camera: High and wide, pulling up and back

shots.action: Rook on the ridge of the thatched roof, arms folded, hat brim low, the black swell rising behind him. He tips his head at us, eyes half shut; the young man grips the rail below
Dawn from high up: one small hut on an empty sea, long light, nothing else in any direction. He turns slowly at the rail, looking

Bright day, a week earlier. The camera swings round the hut on its raft of planks and blue drums: one rope runs from the corner post down into the water. He sits on the edge, feet over the side, kicking slowly, looking round at nothing
Rook strolls along the deck, deadpan, flipping a gold coin and watching it; beyond him the boy sits at the edge and looks at the horizon
shots.camera: Tracking beside him along the deck

shots.action: Low at the corner post: the rope, tight and humming, goes down into the water. The camera lifts to show the hut it holds; he walks across the deck
shots.hud: A ROMPONG: A FLOATING FISH TRAP

shots.action: A card: a drawn chart. A coast on the left, a dotted line running out to a small hut mark with one rope under it, the figure counting up to 125 KM
Dusk. He bends over the generator and pulls its cord, twice; the lamps come on one after another. On the roof Rook's head snaps to each bright bulb and his hat hops
shots.camera: From off the corner of the raft, easing in

shots.action: Night, from above: the lamps throw a pool of light on the black water and silver fish come into it, circling tighter. He leans on the rail and watches them
A card: the little hut under its lamp on a night sea. SINCE HE WAS 16, then ABOUT $130 A MONTH

The weekly boat comes alongside: a narrow hull with outriggers. The boatman lifts a water jug up to him and he crouches at the edge to take it; a crate of fish and a sack wait on the deck. Rook, chin in hand, cannot stop looking at the fish
Night under the eave lamp: he sits by the doorway with the walkie-talkie at his mouth, talking, the set's green light blinking; far lamps on the water behind
Night, high and wide: his three lamps in front, and the lamps of the other huts scattered over the black water to the horizon
Rook on the roof ridge, the far lamps behind him. He points at them one by one, counting, gives up, turns to us and shrugs
Storm. Very close on the post: the rope bar-tight and shaking, strands starting to spring out of it. He crouches over it, eyes wide, one hand out
The same moment from further round: the rope parts and whips, the hut lurches off its mooring and he throws his arms out
shots.camera: Low from the sea, further round

shots.action: A card in two halves: 1ST TIME, ADRIFT A WEEK and 2ND TIME, ADRIFT TWO DAYS. Each time a small boat comes in to the hut mark and FOUND is stamped under it

Dawn after the storm, the broken rope trailing. He sits on the edge with a hand over his eyes, turning his head along the horizon, looking back the way the wind has brought him. Behind him Rook taps his beak
shots.camera: Low from the sea, easing in

shots.action: From high up, the other side: the hut, alone, the sea empty to the horizon. He stands at the rail and turns right round
shots.camera: Very high, from the other side

shots.action: A card: a chart. The other huts' lamps sit in a cluster off the coast; one hut mark is blown away from them, up the sheet, leaving a dotted track. NO BOAT COMES
Inside the hut: a water jug, a small sack and a gas bottle on a shelf. He takes the jug down and tips it; two drops fall. His brows drop
shots.camera: Chest height in the doorway, moving in

shots.action: In the doorway: the stove's blue flame shrinks and goes out under the pot. He lifts the gas bottle and shakes it by his ear: nothing
He sits on the edge with a hand line and jerks a silver fish out of the water, eyes wide. Rook, hand at his chin beside him, snaps his head to the shiny fish; his hat hops
He lifts a rail pulled from the fence, brings it down across his raised knee and it breaks in two; splinters fly. Half the fence behind him is already gone
Dusk. A small fire of fence wood in a cut-down tin; he crouches and holds the fish over it on a stick, eyes heavy. Rook warms both wings at the flames, then taps his beak, thinking
Rain. He stands in it with the jug held up in both hands and his head back, mouth open. Beside him Rook pulls his hat brim down and takes it
A dry day. At the edge he pulls a soaked cloth up out of the sea and wrings it over a cup, both fists turning; water runs out of it
Close: he lifts the wet cloth in both hands, tips his head back and sips from it, eyes shut; drops run off it
shots.camera: Close on his face and hands

shots.action: Rook holds the cup under his beak, pulls his head back, and turns it upside down over the side; the water falls out
Grey water, low: a dark fin cuts across in front of the raft. On the deck he backs away from the edge, arms out, eyes wide
shots.camera: Very low on the water, sliding

shots.action: From straight above: the long shape goes round the raft. He turns in the middle of the deck to keep it in front of him. On the roof Rook leans over to look and loses a feather
Late afternoon. He sits against the hut's corner post with a small book open in both hands, head down over it, lips moving. Rook sits apart, facing the sea, then turns his head to him
A card: a sun crosses the sky over and over above the little hut, and the day count climbs
Close on Rook, sitting. He looks across at the boy, then down, and pulls his hat brim over his eyes. No joke
A ship on the horizon. He jumps at the rail and points at it with his whole arm, mouth open
shots.camera: Behind him on the deck, looking out

shots.action: Seen from the sea: he waves a pale cloth over his head with both arms, hopping, shouting. Beside him Rook waves an orange rag of his own, beak open
Dusk, from out on the water: he stands at the back corner with a lit lantern held high, swinging it over his head, mouth open
The long hull slides across the horizon and keeps going. His arms come down and his head drops. Rook lowers his rag and pulls his hat brim over his eyes
Night. A long lit hull goes by far off, as big as a street. In front of it, very small, the hut, and a lantern being waved
A card: ship after ship crosses, each one struck through in red, the count climbing past ten: 10+ SHIPS, NONE STOPPED
Night, a quiet sea, a low fire. He sits with his arms round his knees and his head down, shoulders shaking. Rook sits beside him, turns his head to him, brows sad, and says nothing
The same night from very high, turning: one small raft with a small fire on it, and black water in every direction
Dawn. Another ship, nearer than the others, crossing. He lifts the cloth again with one tired arm
shots.camera: Behind him on the deck, looking out

shots.action: A card: a chart. The hut's dotted track runs from North Sulawesi, 14 JULY, across the sheet to a small island, GUAM, 31 AUGUST. DAY 49
Dawn, from above the ship: its deck and hatch covers slide through the frame, and down past its side the hut is small on the water with a small figure on it, waving
shots.camera: High over the ship, travelling with it

shots.action: From the other side: he waves the cloth with both arms; Rook waves his rag. Nothing changes
shots.camera: From the water, the other side

shots.action: Close, inside the hut: his hand closes on the radio on the shelf and lifts it; the dial turns and a green light starts to blink
Close: the radio at his mouth, he shouts into it, eyes wide. Rook leans in and jabs a wing at the set; his hat hops
The radio still at his chin, the green light blinking, his head turned to the ship's stern, which is still going away
shots.camera: Over the radio to the far ship

shots.action: The ship's bridge. The mate at the radio set stops with a hand in the air, the set's light blinking; he spins to the captain and points out of the windows. The captain's head comes up
From above the hut: far off, the ship leans into a turn, foam curving behind it, until its bow points at us. On the roof Rook's hat leaves his head; the young man jumps with both arms up
shots.camera: High over the roof, looking out

shots.action: The hull stands over the hut like a wall and the grey swell between them heaves; crew in orange lean over the rail, pointing down. He waves both arms up at them
shots.camera: Very low on the water, looking up, rolling

shots.action: Grey, from very high: the ship goes round the raft in a wide ring, its wake drawn on the sea behind it. The count: pass 1, 2, 3, 4
From the ship's deck: a crewman winds up and heaves a line. It uncoils through the air and drops into the water short of the hut. He reaches up for it
shots.camera: Over the crew's shoulders, looking down

shots.action: Close on him at the edge: he looks down at the water, up at the ship, sets his jaw and bends his knees. Rook, beside him, looks from him to the water and back
He goes off the edge of the raft towards the line, arms out, and hits the water in a burst of spray. Rook flaps up off the roof, beak open, and loses a feather
In the swell between raft and hull: he swims, arm over arm, for the rope in the water; the ship's side is a wall ahead. Rook flaps along above him
At the ship's side: he climbs the rope ladder in the spray, one arm stretched up; a crewman hangs over the rail and catches his hand
shots.camera: Low on the water, tilting up the hull

shots.action: On deck in low sun: he sits on a hatch cover with a towel round his shoulders and takes a cup from a crouching crewman; his face eases. Another crewman stands by. Rook sits on the rail, watching, brows soft
shots.camera: Chest height on the deck, easing in

shots.action: The same hatch cover: the ship's cook, in white, snips at his hair with scissors and bits of it fall; he smiles. On the rail Rook claps both hands onto his own hat
The bridge again, from the other end: the captain with a handset at his mouth, talking and nodding; the mate, hands on hips, looks back along the deck
shots.camera: Along the console, the other way

shots.action: Dusk, wide: the ship carries him off towards the low sun. The hut is left behind in the foreground, empty, turning slowly
A card: a chart. The ship's dotted line runs north from Guam to a harbour marked on a coast: TOKUYAMA, 6 SEPTEMBER 2018

A quay in grey morning light: the ship alongside like a wall, a gangway down to the concrete. He walks down it; two people in dark clothes wait at its foot and one of them waves. Rook sits on a bollard
shots.camera: Wide along the quay, moving in

shots.action: At the foot of the gangway: he steps onto the quay and an official takes his hand in both of his; the other, with a folder, smiles. Behind them Rook touches his hat
Home. On the sand in front of a house on stilts his mother runs to him and gets both arms round him; his father puts a hand on his shoulder. Palms move behind them
shots.camera: Low from the shore, easing in

shots.action: Rook, a few steps off under a palm, arms folded, watching the three of them. His brows go soft and he touches his hat brim
He walks up the beach towards us, away from the water, and does not look back. Behind him Rook stands at the waterline looking out to sea, then turns and follows
shots.camera: Side on, tracking along the beach

shots.action: Rook at the edge of the water, the empty sea behind him. He looks over his shoulder at it, turns back to us, lifts both wings and lets them drop
Rook back on the empty raft at dusk. He turns to us and shrugs, brows soft
Rook's case board, weathered planks lashed with rope: a photograph of the young man waving at a far ship. CASE 019, 49 DAYS IN A HUT, stamped TRUE
Once more, wide from the water: the small figure on the raft, both arms up, the cloth going
He picks a bright fish hook off the planks, turns it in the last light, pockets it and pulls his hat brim down
